body:
## Purpose

This PR follows up on #4934 by targeting global memory reads, using the AMIP target configuration (`numerics_sphere_he16ze79.yml` + `amip_target.yml`) as the reference: it fuses the functions with the most global loads per timestep into slice loops whose intermediate values are register temporaries, and deletes 32 of the 64 scratch fields that `temporary_quantities` can allocate. Floating-point operations are reordered where that saves reads, so results change at the level of roundoff, and the reproducibility counter is bumped to 467.

## Disclosure

This PR and its description were mostly generated using Claude.

## Content

- `edmfx_sgs_diffusive_flux_tendency!`, which has the most global loads per timestep on `main`: the scalar fluxes of the environment and every updraft run in one column loop, and the TKE and momentum fluxes in another. The horizontal SGS fluxes run in 4 kernels instead of 57.
- `horizontal_advection_tendency!`: the horizontal dynamics, the horizontal tracer advection, and the vertical vorticity and Coriolis terms of `uₕ` share one slab loop; `viscous_sponge_tendency!`, `edmfx_entr_detr_tendency!`, and `hgrad_invariants!` run in one or two loops each.
- AMD: `amd_tendency!` replaces the horizontal and vertical tendencies, in 7 kernels instead of 74.
- `initialize_implicit_stage_problem!`: the `u₃`, `ρa`, and tracer solves of each draft, the updraft sedimentation, and the end of each Picard round run in column loops.
- Jacobian: the SGS advection, SGS mass flux, diffusion (of every closure), and SGS diffusion and entrainment blocks are each built in one column loop.
- Non-orographic gravity wave drag runs in a few fused loops, and its forcing is clamped once per `dt_nogw` callback, so the `utendnogw` and `vtendnogw` diagnostics report the clamped forcing.
- Loops over the updrafts run in one kernel for all of them, and `constrain_state!`, the microphysics caches and tendencies, and several smaller functions keep their intermediate values in registers or lazy expressions instead of scratch fields.
- `set_explicit_precomputed_quantities!` skips the state-dependent sedimentation velocities, which `set_implicit_precomputed_quantities_core!` already sets.
- The draft and grid-mean precomputed quantities, water advection, hyperdiffusion, the SGS mass flux, and the explicit vertical advection keep `main`'s kernels, since their fused versions run slower on an A100 under Julia 1.13, whose kernels keep the parameter structs they capture in local memory (until CliMA/ClimaParams.jl#345).

## Comparison against main

The PR rows of the two tables below come from builds of the head of this PR, `3a7af3427`. The AMIP `main` rows come from `main` at `7eacbde07`, the base of this PR, and the CI `main` rows from the merge-queue build of #4973 (`3f48a5487`, before #4968), the latest that runs the full CI. The aggregate rows compare the jobs that passed in both builds and ran for over a minute; their values and changes are the minimum, median, and maximum over jobs. Most of the added AMIP compilation time is in the first coupling step, which compiles for 6.5 min against 5.9 min on `main`.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flagship AMIP (A100), wall time per coupling step | 9.03 s | 13.22 s | -31.7% | [465](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-end-to-end-performance/builds/465), [453](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-end-to-end-performance/builds/453) |
| Prognostic EDMF aquaplanet (P100), `T_exp!` min time | 23.1 ms | 27.4 ms | -15.8% | [32603](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-ci/builds/32603), [32584](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-ci/builds/32584) |
| Prognostic EDMF aquaplanet (P100), `T_imp!` min time | 5.10 ms | 7.28 ms | -29.9% | [32603](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-ci/builds/32603), [32584](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-ci/builds/32584) |

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Flagship AMIP (A100), compilation time | 18.3 min | 17.8 min | +2.9% | [465](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-end-to-end-performance/builds/465), [453](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-end-to-end-performance/builds/453) |
| Flagship AMIP (A100), compilation memory | 259.0 GiB | 247.8 GiB | +4.5% | [465](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-end-to-end-performance/builds/465), [453](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-end-to-end-performance/builds/453) |
| ClimaAtmos GPU jobs, wall time (19 jobs) | 1.8 / 20.3 / 26.9 min | 1.8 / 17.3 / 24.9 min | +3.0% / +5.9% / +32.8% | [32603](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-ci/builds/32603), [32584](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-ci/builds/32584) |

The table below splits the device time of a flagship AMIP coupling step on an A100, its DRAM traffic (reads plus writes), and its global load and store instructions into components that do not overlap ([464](https://buildkite.com/clima/climaatmos-end-to-end-performance/builds/464), with `a86ca53e0`, whose code is identical to the head of this PR, and `7eacbde07` on `main`). Times are averages over 20 traced coupling steps, which include one radiation call, and the DRAM traffic, loads, and stores are from Nsight Compute on one coupling step without radiation, plus those of the RRTMGP kernels of the radiation call divided by 20. Under Julia 1.13, most of the DRAM traffic of both branches is local memory, since kernels keep the parameter structs they capture on the stack.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

| `set_implicit_precomputed_quantities!` | 472.2 ms (5.2%) | +0.1% | 548.4 GB (5.2%) | -0.1% | 5684.8 / 1004.6 M (8.9% / 10.2%) | +0.3% / +1.8% |
| `correct_implicit_advection_tendency!` | 340.4 ms (3.8%) | no change | 402.3 GB (3.8%) | no change | 1764.5 / 284.5 M (2.8% / 2.9%) | no change |
| surface models (land, ocean, sea ice) | 44.6 ms (0.5%) | -1.0% | 50.9 GB (0.5%) | no change | 454.8 / 133.9 M (0.7% / 1.3%) | no change |

| other atmos (`constrain_state!`, other kernels) | 1.1 ms (0.0%) | -20.9% | 0.5 GB (0.0%) | -49.8% | 160.8 / 91.4 M (0.3% / 0.9%) | -46.3% / -11.2% |

title: Eliminate global caches through column loop fusion
